topicName: Linear Models: LinearRegression, Ridge, Lasso, and ElasticNet
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Linear Models in Scikit-learn: LinearRegression, Ridge, Lasso, and ElasticNet"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Linear models are foundational tools in machine learning. They assume a linear relationship between the input features and the target variable. Scikit-learn provides a robust suite of linear models, ranging from standard Ordinary Least Squares to regularized variants designed to handle multicollinearity and prevent overfitting."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Ordinary Least Squares (LinearRegression)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"LinearRegression fits a linear model with coefficients w = (w1, ..., wp) to minimize the residual sum of squares between the observed targets in the dataset and the targets predicted by the linear approximation."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Sample data
X = np.array([[1, 1], [1, 2], [2, 2], [2, 3]])
y = np.dot(X, np.array([1, 2])) + 3

# Initialize and fit model
reg = LinearRegression()
reg.fit(X, y)
print("Coefficients:", reg.coef_)
print("Intercept:", reg.intercept_)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Ridge Regression (L2 Regularization)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ridge regression addresses some of the problems of Ordinary Least Squares by imposing a penalty on the size of the coefficients. The penalty is proportional to the square of the value of the coefficients (L2 penalty)."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge

# Initialize and fit Ridge model with alpha=1.0
ridge = Ridge(alpha=1.0)
ridge.fit(X, y)
print("Ridge Coefficients:", ridge.coef_)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Lasso Regression (L1 Regularization)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Lasso is a linear model that estimates sparse coefficients. It uses an L1 penalty, which forces some coefficients to be exactly zero, effectively performing feature selection."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.linear_model import Lasso

# Initialize and fit Lasso model
lasso = Lasso(alpha=0.1)
lasso.fit(X, y)
print("Lasso Coefficients:", lasso.coef_)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. ElasticNet (L1 and L2 Regularization)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"ElasticNet is a linear regression model trained with both L1 and L2 prior as regularizer. This combination allows for learning a sparse model like Lasso, while maintaining the regularization properties of Ridge."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNet

# Initialize and fit ElasticNet model
elastic_net = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, l1_ratio=0.5)
elastic_net.fit(X, y)
print("ElasticNet Coefficients:", elastic_net.coef_)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Regularization Techniques"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LinearRegression: No regularization, prone to overfitting when features are collinear."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ridge (L2): Shrinks coefficients towards zero, handles multicollinearity well."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Lasso (L1): Drives irrelevant coefficients to zero, performs automatic feature selection."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ElasticNet: Combines L1 and L2 penalties, ideal when there are multiple correlated features."}]
